name: Roy Cooper
subject: Please endorse my campaign for U.S. Senate →
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Roy Cooper for North Carolina
body:
Before politics, before party and before power, I will always put the people of North Carolina first.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6532?source=&t=1&akid=772%2E124072%2ESY-cDt)
| | | |
---
Peter – over the past couple of weeks, I’ve been out on the road meeting with North Carolinians directly on the Make Stuff Cost Less tour. They tell me versions of the same thing:
⛽ Gas prices are spiking, and it’s costing more to put food on the table.

🩺 They can’t keep up with skyrocketing health insurance costs and get the care they need.

🇺🇲 They’re fed up with the chaos in Washington, DC, and they’re worried about the future of our country.
I know we can do better. That’s why I’m in this fight.

**Before politics, before party and before power, I will always put the people of North Carolina first – as I’ve done my entire career in public service. As Governor:**
✅ I expanded Medicaid for hundreds of thousands of working North Carolinians.

✅ I created hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs.

✅ I increased teacher pay and expanded paid parental leave.
**Now, I’m ready to fight in the Senate for working families – but getting there won’t be easy. The GOP is going all in to defeat me, and I need to know that folks like you are in my corner.**
**[Will you add your name now to personally endorse my campaign for U.S. Senate? I’m looking for 10,000 signatures before midnight, and I’m hoping I can count on you. It would really mean a lot.](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/endorse-cooper-2026-email?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk54-su-nd&t=7&akid=772%2E124072%2ESY-cDt)**
| | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/endorse-cooper-2026-email?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk54-su-nd&t=8&akid=772%2E124072%2ESY-cDt)
---
Thank you,

Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

subject: Federal court blocks RFK’s vaccine changes – please read

body:
https://kellyforcongress.org [https://kellyforcongress.org]
Hi Peter,
Kelly Morrison here. I wanted to reach out to share some good news from earlier this week – a federal judge blocked RFK Jr.’s changes to vaccine policies.
Screenshot of an article from The Hill that titled [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP59/1/109390/images/screenshots/courts-block-rfk.png]
RFK Jr. has launched relentless attacks on the life-saving vaccines and decades of medical research that have kept millions of Americans healthy. That's why as soon as I got to Congress, I joined my colleagues in forming the first Democratic Doctors Caucus. We have been on the front lines calling for RFK Jr.’s resignation and working to combat the barrage of misinformation spouted by him and this administration.
This ruling is a step in the right direction. There is so much else we need to focus on to make America healthy – from preventing disease, to investing in medical and scientific research, to reducing chronic illness. RFK Jr’s policies and constant political attacks only set us back on making progress on these issues.
Peter, the only way to put some checks on RFK Jr and this administration is to flip the U.S. House this November. I am laser-focused on doing everything I can to hold my seat and support targeted Congressional races across the Midwest, and I believe that together, we will flip the House.
In just under two weeks, we will have our first end of quarter fundraising deadline of this election year. We have ambitious organizing goals this year, and we set a goal of raising $14,000 before the end of this month to finish this quarter strong.

name: Fran
subject: They're dropping out of politics
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
But we can win them over
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260319-2629)
Peter,
The Trump coalition is imploding.
New survey [data](https://act.francescahong.com/go/6757?t=1&akid=2629%2E105371%2EEvUOkS) out this week from the Center for Working-Class Politics shows that one in five Trump 2024 voters is walking away from the Republican Party. Among his poorest supporters, it's nearly one in three.
These people [aren't becoming Democrats](https://act.francescahong.com/go/6758?t=2&akid=2629%2E105371%2EEvUOkS) — they're dropping out of politics entirely because they've decided nobody is coming to help.
But here's the thing: they're winnable. They're not voting based on party. They went for Trump because they were angry with the status quo. They're looking for someone who will actually fight for working people, someone who takes their lives seriously.
That's us. That's this campaign. We're leading the Democratic primary field because we have the clearest vision and the best plan to create permanent affordability in Wisconsin. Our core policies — universal child care; paid leave for all; better, fairer, cheaper healthcare — provide real solutions for working-class voters.
With 65% of Wisconsin voters still undecided, the door is wide open. The path to the governorship runs through the people both parties have left behind.
We're running to build a Wisconsin where working people can actually get ahead — where child care doesn't eat your whole paycheck, where you can see a doctor without going into debt, and where a full-time job means you can afford to stay in your community.
When people hear our message, they get on board. But we need a bigger megaphone.
[Chip in what you can — $5, $10, $100 — to help us reach voters across the state.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260319.byEzrq&refcode=em20260319-2629&t=3&akid=2629%2E105371%2EEvUOkS)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260319.byEzrq&amount=5&refcode=em20260319-2629&t=22&akid=2629%2E105371%2EEvUOkS)**

Fran

They're looking for someone who will actually fight for working people, someone who takes their lives seriously. That's us. That's this campaign. [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
This week, J.D. Vance paid Michigan a visit, and his speech proved, yet
again, how out of touch he and the entire Trump administration are from
everyday Michiganders. His entire visit was filled with more empty
promises.

As I’ve traveled around the state, I’ve heard from Michiganders who voted
for Trump and Vance because they promised to lower prices and bring down
costs. Those promises were broken.

Instead, Medicaid is getting cut. Reckless tariffs are driving up the cost
of everything. Gas prices are rising, creating an extra bill for
Michiganders.

J.D. Vance doesn’t seem to care that the challenges working families are
facing are directly caused by his own choices.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3483?t=1001&akid=1564%2E181023%2E9ZU8zl ]I’m running for Governor to make Michigan the best place to be a kid,
raise a kid, and call home. I hope you’ll join me in the fight to make
Michigan a place where everyone can thrive. Can you chip in $5 or $10
today to make sure we have the resources to win?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3484?t=1002&akid=1564%2E181023%2E9ZU8zl ]Donate $5 →

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3489?t=1007&akid=1564%2E181023%2E9ZU8zl ]Other →

Michigan deserves better than empty visits from the people who caused the
mess we find ourselves in.

If J.D. Vance really cared about making his visit productive, he would
have spoken with one of the 350,000 Michiganders who are losing healthcare
because of his administration or the hardworking parents who are forced to
pinch pennies at the gas pump.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3483?t=1008&akid=1564%2E181023%2E9ZU8zl ]I’m not running to give empty promises, I’m ready to continue fighting
back against anyone — no matter how powerful — who takes advantage of
Michiganders. But I can’t do this without your help. Can you pitch in

Thank you,
Jocelyn Benson

Because when we stand together, we are stronger. When we turn fear into courage and anger into action, we are unstoppable.

name: Teichert in the Trenches
subject: 💥Your Leadership Tree💥
body:
We are in the midst of an exciting college basketball season
---
| | | | | |
---
| | **💥****Your Leadership Tree****💥**
---
We are in the midst of an exciting college basketball season and the men’s NCAA basketball tourney begins in earnest today. Thus, it’s the perfect time to share one of my favorite leadership lessons – one that uses a basketball analogy.
The lesson is derived from a brilliant leadership book – _Duke Sucks: A Completely Evenhanded, Unbiased Investigation Into the Most Evil Team on Planet Earth_. **Evenhanded** and **unbiased** are in the subtitle, so we should believe every word!
Now before you give up on me here – even if you are a Duke fan (Kevin!) – please stick it out. Even if you don’t like the analogy, the application is stunningly relevant to all.
CHARGE #14 in the book claims the following: Duke’s **Coaching Tree** Is Not Exactly a Mighty Oak.
So what is a **coaching tree**? The concept is simple. A coach’s influence is far greater than just wins and losses in a particular season. Their actual impact is rightfully measured by how they develop players to become coaches themselves. In doing so, their impact is multiplied as their trunk yields branches and leaves. Their legacy isn’t solely defined by a singular season, and their impact is multi-generational. It requires deliberate and intentional investment to look beyond the current season to develop coaching capabilities that endure.
The book describes Coach Dean Smith from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (the authors are UNC fans which no doubt lies at the core of their hatred of Duke). “During the 2008 NBA season, nearly a quarter of the coaches could trace their lineage back to Smith.” Even with his coaching days behind him, Smith’s impact endured. He had intentionally and deliberately invested in raising up basketball leaders, and as a result, his coaching tree was flourishing.
Let me provide a more modern example from college football. All four coaches of the national semi-finalist teams in 2026 had been assistants under Coach Nick Saban at Alabama (Roll Tide!). Even with his coaching days behind him, Saban’s impact endures. He had intentionally and deliberately invested in raising up football leaders, and as a result, his coaching tree is flourishing.
What does _Duke Sucks_ say about Coach K of Duke?
“So, what’s left of this [coaching] tree after firings, probations, NCAA investigations, allegations of falsifying drug tests, and lots and lots of losing? There are no more branches. All the leaves have fallen. **Verdict.** Guilty. **The K coaching tree is nothing more than a rotting, smelly stump in the middle of a lonely field.** ”
Now before you give up on the most important part, PLEASE KEEP READING even if you don’t concur with the Verdict described above!
Leaders of all types have their own version of a coaching tree ... **a leadership tree**.
A leader’s influence is far greater than just success or failure during the leader’s tenure. Their actual impact is rightfully measured by how they develop subordinates to become leaders themselves. In doing so, their impact is multiplied as their trunk yields branches and leaves. Their legacy isn’t solely defined by a singular time period, and their impact is multi-generational. It requires deliberate and intentional investment to look beyond the here-and-now to develop leadership capabilities that endure.
So how is your leadership tree?! Is it thriving like the coaching trees of Coach Smith and Coach Saban, or is it withering like Coach K’s?
It’s not too late!
Reshift your priorities to intentionally and deliberately invest in others to create multi-generational success and enduring impact, and most importantly, to ensure that your leadership tree avoids the stigma of being nothing more than a rotting, smelly stump in the middle of a lonely field.
Intentionally and deliberately investing in others will allow you to LEAD WELL – with multi-generational impact!

* John

| | | | **Teichert in the Trenches**

body:
Make Signs for No Kings Day! Meet Neighbors!

| |
---
| | My campaign is built on faith in the process of fair elections and the belief that we can only rebuild a functional democracy by talking directly with our neighbors about the issues that matter in our daily lives. We can all learn. We can all change. Together, we can defeat the algorithms designed to divide and distract us while billionaires pick our pockets and destroy everything we need to thrive. _Even if we disagree about the wisdom and efficacy of redistricting, we agree that change is needed in Washington._ I am committed to continuing conversations about real issues as we await the referendum results. We must emerge from this referendum process ready to work together for substantive change on the policies that have created the largest wealth gap in US history, the threat of continued entanglement in foreign wars, and the catastrophic destruction of our environment. I don't know about you, but I want a break from the partisan frenzy around the redistricting vote. **If you live near Weyers Cave, please join us on March 27 for a potluck starting at 5 PM.** Live music provided by _The Broken Hearts_ starts at 6 PM. We will also be making signs for the No Kings protests on March 28, because voting is essential, but so is defending democracy on the streets. RSVP [here.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/49rqMEuqmGoNTJrXZ9n3sg~~/AAUS1hA~/xBiw_g3ezBdmTDn4OHY_3qkkRxM44qb-LN8OBbK4q8kcYg1qr0Fwn9twjayJ0Cu0qcs7KcYcLA1SBCQ6SErF72r6sfx_acxU_M5wpYgF8Ru3y1pO9H_HamahNHirKZQ0eGnB2c2BFVmc3q_AJp9LZ7O7fYs_ctcjh6gk_mnvv0zEiTsw51tD934jXgT5iqqEw8mrETMubxX3E9QJFlQSlzZH_KZgX11uGUL6HIE0oHv1SMPk6M0djsw_M-HdgC225MU1shFcwrUKRKqU_Vc2JQ~~) If you are unable to attend, but want to support the cause, you can also make a contribution using that link. **Please bring:**
* Food to share and your potluck plates and cutlery.
* Your beverage of choice.
* Chairs to sit around the bonfire in the field.
* Sign-making supplies, if you have them. We will provide some supplies.
* A sweatshirt or jacket — we are really gathering in the barn!

If you live too far from Weyers Cave, please try to have at least one conversation with a neighbor about a policy that needs to change to improve their life. Look for a No Kings demonstration near you. And, don't forget to vote in the referendum. Onward!

name: Katie Britt (R-AL)
subject: This is my story.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Britt for Alabama, Inc
body:
From dance classes and a hardware store to the Senate.
|
---
| | | | [](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
---
| | |
---
| | Patriot,
My name is Katie Britt, and if it’s alright with you, I’d like to share a little about who I am. **I’m not part of the D.C. cocktail circuit, and I never will be._That’s just not who I am._**

In 2022, I was elected to represent the great state of Alabama in the United States Senate. I became the first woman in Alabama’s history to hold this seat—but that’s not why I ran.

I ran because I’m a _**mom**_ , a _**wife**_ , and a _**conservative**_ who’s fed up with the direction this country is heading. I came to Washington to fight for our families, to protect our values, and to bring some Alabama backbone to a broken system.

I didn’t come here to make friends with the political elite. I came here to stand up for the people who don’t have a voice in the room—and I’m not backing down.
---
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Before coming to the Senate, I served as the first female president and CEO of the Business Council of Alabama, and before that, I was Chief of Staff to Senator Richard Shelby. **I’ve never shied away from a challenge—and I’ve never forgotten who I’m fighting for.** In every role I’ve held, my mission has been the same: _deliver real results for Alabama families and the American people._
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Before starting my career in public service, I earned my undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Alabama. That experience taught me how to lead, think on my feet, and fight for what I believe in—**and it laid the foundation for _everything_ I’ve done since.**
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
But long before that, I was just a small-town girl from Enterprise, Alabama. My dad ran the local hardware store. My mom taught dance to almost every kid in town. We didn’t grow up with wealth or political connections. **We came from hard work, grit, and doing things the right way._That’s how I was raised, and that’s exactly how I lead._**
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
My husband Wesley and our two amazing kids are my rock. In 2011, a tornado tore through our home and nearly took our lives. That moment changed everything, and reminded me what truly matters. __**Faith** , **family** , and **resilience**.__
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
I’ve lived a life full of hard work, determination, and breaking barriers. There have been challenges and triumphs alike, but I wouldn’t trade any of it.

My story is a testament to what America stands for—the American Dream. From a small town in Alabama, I rose to become my state’s U.S. Senator—a woman who’s breaking barriers and fighting for conservative values every day.

_**_I’m living proof of the limitless opportunity and freedom that define this country._**_

But, I didn’t get here by playing it safe or staying quiet, **and I’m not about to start now.**

The radical Left wants to _silence_ conservatives like me. They want to drown out our voices and push their agenda without opposition, but I’m standing firm.

I’m fighting tooth and nail to keep up and push back hard, for Alabama, for our values, and for every American who believes in freedom.

**The support I’ve received so far means everything, but this fight is far from over.** We need the resources to keep going strong and hold our ground.

**[So, after hearing a bit of my story, will you take a moment to chip in whatever you can afford to help me keep up this fight? The road ahead won’t be easy, but I’ve faced tough battles before. And it would mean the world to have you standing with me.](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)**
|
---
[CHIP IN TO FIGHT WITH KATIE BRITT >>](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
Thank you, and may God bless America.

Katie Britt (R-AL)
|
---
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
| | ****

---
|
---
|
---
|
---
[](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|
---
I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong.

_**Faith. Family. Freedom.**_

The Left is doing everything they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored.

From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul.

**This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.**

Will you stand with me?
|
---
[STAND WITH KATIE >>](https://link.email.brittforsenate.)
|

I'm a pediatrician. I’m pissed. I’m scared. And I need your help to defeat Lindsey Graham in the U.S. Senate.
I’m not the “monsters-under-the-bed” kind of scared. I’m the “I’ve watched children suffer from preventable illness and injury while politicians do absolutely nothing” kind of scared.
I’ve treated kids who’ve been shot. Kids whose families struggle to afford their medications.
Kids who live with mold that causes asthma attacks, miss school for climate disasters, and watch politicians use them as political pawns.
And now? Trump is causing chaos and Lindsey Graham is right by his side.
And Medicaid — the program that keeps half our pediatric patients insured, healthy, and...alive — is on the chopping block to pay for tax breaks for billionaires.
So yeah, I never planned to run for Senate.
But I’m scared. I’m pissed. I’m motivated. And I’m 100% in.
I’m running for Senate in South Carolina to defeat Lindsey Graham and to fight for the kids no one in D.C. seems to be thinking about. So I need you with me.
We need to hit 10,000 donations before midnight to prove that this campaign can go the distance. Can I count on you to split a donation with my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
HELP ME DEFEAT LINDSEY GRAHAM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]
I’m running because the Republican Party, led by people like Lindsey Graham, is dismantling the very systems that keep our kids safe here in South Carolina.
I’m running because the issues I care about — children’s healthcare, vaccines, gun violence, public education, Social Security, Medicaid and Medicare — are under direct attack right now.
And I’m running because I consider it my professional duty as a pediatrician — to give children a strong voice at the national level. Too many are comfortable on the sidelines. That won’t work for me.
We need bold leaders who aren’t afraid to fight. I am ready.
Even though the path will be hard, I know Lindsey Graham must be held accountable. He certainly doesn’t deserve a free pass back to D.C. for six more years.
That’s why I’m running for US Senate. To defeat Trump’s lapdog and fight for everyday Americans. But, I need your support today. Can you rush a split donation of $10 (or whatever you can spare) between Resist Reclaim Rebuild and me to become a Founding Donor to my campaign? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-annieandrews]

Thank you for believing in this campaign,
Dr. Annie Andrews

name: Forward Party
subject: What Virginia’s Redistricting Vote Means for Voters
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
A key moment for fair maps and voter trust

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
Early voting is now underway in Virginia. On April 21, voters will decide whether to allow a mid-decade redraw of congressional maps, revisiting a system designed to limit direct political control. In 2020, Virginia adopted a redistricting commission made up of legislators and citizens, evenly split between Republicans and Democrats. The maps drawn after the last census were intended to last through 2031, providing consistency and predictability for voters. The current measure would temporarily change that system. It would allow the General Assembly to redraw congressional districts before the next census, with a new map already approved that would take effect for the 2026 elections if voters agree. Supporters say this allows Virginia to respond to similar moves in other states. Opponents, including the Forward Party, are concerned it could reintroduce more direct political influence into a process voters intended to make more independent. Below is our official statement This moment in Virginia reflects a broader national challenge. Across the country, both parties have increasingly looked to redraw maps in ways that strengthen their position, raising questions about consistency and trust in the rules that govern elections. As Brian Vincent, Forward-aligned independent mayor of Farmville, Virginia, recently wrote, stable rules and clear standards are essential to building public confidence. You can read his full perspective [here.](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=aWgihZZNkxzzsLrsJs6WiFEYodViZQ2K7mDj4GIdMyUNfPZgnA6fp4lCRugytua_aw_adpPzs0lqPk38K7WkKUlMrhIqommPiXzeyi8BCnzC0NnU91y-YkV_X1O40uJ3J3YvG6EJSDdOB4OJsopQuA&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_4a&n=1)

[](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=aWgihZZNkxzzsLrsJs6WiFEYodViZQ2K7mDj4GIdMyUNfPZgnA6fp4lCRugytua_aw_adpPzs0lqPk38K7WkKUlMrhIqommPiXzeyi8BCnzC0NnU91y-YkV_X1O40uJ3J3YvG6EJSDdOB4OJsopQuA&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_4a&n=2)That same principle was echoed by Lindsey Drath, CEO of the Forward Party, in a recent [Fox 5 DC interview](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_KeSraPW0gSlxEBMOvJrEouH4SjeZmYtvTWulgNFAfahO9dslyVyqYmJy2rwR-z_&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_4a&n=3), where she emphasized that voters want a system that is fair, transparent, and consistent over time.

How districts are drawn shapes how elections function, from how competitive races are to how responsive leaders are to the people they represent. At Forward, we believe the goal should be simple: fair processes, consistent rules, and elections where voters feel their voices truly matter. Virginia voters will make their decision soon, but this issue goes well beyond one state. Across the country, rules like gerrymandering, closed primaries, and complicated ballot access requirements often shape who gets to run and who voters actually get to choose from. Too often, they narrow the field instead of opening it up. That can leave independent voters with fewer real options and make it harder to support leaders who truly reflect their values or make them feel proud to cast a ballot. It also keeps a lot of strong civic leaders on the sidelines. Many people who have led in their communities, businesses, or public service simply do not want to sign up for strict party labels or ideological lines just to run for office. If we want a healthier democracy, it starts with making sure the system invites more people in, not keeps them out, and gives voters real choices they can believe in. **Please forward this to your friends, family, and coworkers. It helps us introduce them to Forward and to what we are building. Also consider inviting them to one of our upcoming events listed below. We'd love to meet them.**

clean_body: A key moment for fair maps and voter trust | | | www.forwardparty.com Peter — Early voting is now underway in Virginia. On April 21, voters will decide whether to allow a mid-decade redraw of congressional maps, revisiting a system designed to limit direct political control. In 2020, Virginia adopted a redistricting commission made up of legislators and citizens, evenly split between Republicans and Democrats. The maps drawn after the last census were intended to last through 2031, providing consistency and predictability for voters. The current measure would temporarily change that system. It would allow the General Assembly to redraw congressional districts before the next census, with a new map already approved that would take effect for the 2026 elections if voters agree. Supporters say this allows Virginia to respond to similar moves in other states. Opponents, including the Forward Party, are concerned it could reintroduce more direct political influence into a process voters intended to make more independent. Below is our official statement This moment in Virginia reflects a broader national challenge. Across the country, both parties have increasingly looked to redraw maps in ways that strengthen their position, raising questions about consistency and trust in the rules that govern elections. As Brian Vincent, Forward-aligned independent mayor of Farmville, Virginia, recently wrote, stable rules and clear standards are essential to building public confidence. You can read his full perspective same principle was echoed by Lindsey Drath, CEO of the Forward Party, in a recent , where she emphasized that voters want a system that is fair, transparent, and consistent over time. How districts are drawn shapes how elections function, from how competitive races are to how responsive leaders are to the people they represent. At Forward, we believe the goal should be simple: fair processes, consistent rules, and elections where voters feel their voices truly matter. Virginia voters will make their decision soon, but this issue goes well beyond one state. Across the country, rules like gerrymandering, closed primaries, and complicated ballot access requirements often shape who gets to run and who voters actually get to choose from. Too often, they narrow the field instead of opening it up. That can leave independent voters with fewer real options and make it harder to support leaders who truly reflect their values or make them feel proud to cast a ballot. It also keeps a lot of strong civic leaders on the sidelines. Many people who have led in their communities, businesses, or public service simply do not want to sign up for strict party labels or ideological lines just to run for office. If we want a healthier democracy, it starts with making sure the system invites more people in, not keeps them out, and gives voters real choices they can believe in. body:

Derek — Did you know that over $54 million was bet on prediction markets about whether “Iran’s Ali Khamenei would be out as Supreme Leader”? Or that every day, people are betting on prediction market apps about assassinations, terrorist activity, war, and death? [**There is nothing redeeming about betting on death. No societal benefit is gained. And the most perverse incentives are created. That’s why I introduced legislation to ban prediction contracts based on these sensitive topics of national security concern. Add your name in support of this legislation and help me get it across the finish line →**](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/EG_2603_Deathbets?refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_PET_AC90_20260319_PM2_V1_S1&t=4&akid=9656%2E5257348%2E4u3nyC) | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/EG_2603_Deathbets?refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_PET_AC90_20260319_PM2_V1_S1&t=5&akid=9656%2E5257348%2E4u3nyC)
---
The rapid proliferation of prediction markets and betting on events in real time requires regulation and legislation.
This market has quickly become the newest Wild West, and it has dangerous implications.
Betting on war and death creates an environment in which insiders can profit from classified information, our national security is jeopardized, and violence is encouraged.
There is no justification for gambling on lives — and my legislation, the DEATH BETS Act, will ban these prediction contracts.
In the age of rapid modernization and commodification of the news cycle, legislation like this is vital to make sure we are keeping consumers safe and holding businesses accountable.
[**Sign on in support of the DEATH BETS Act today.**](https://act.adamschiff.com/signup/EG_2603_Deathbets?refcode=AU_ABS_EG_GEN_PET_AC90_20260319_PM2_V1_S1&t=6&akid=9656%2E5257348%2E4u3nyC)

Here's something you may not know about me:

Back in my college years, and even for a bit during my producing days, I was a semi-pro pool player. 🎱 [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127677192/608886318/-2092947258?refcode=em-3.19.26-all-r&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZWE2YWVjNTctZmQyMy1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=dJawhRU0RPxen5hIzsYkz5yDYljriJ0vl8drYJYnLQA=)
Believe it or not, some of the most important skills I developed at the pool table I still use today as a legislator. I learned that people like playing mind games when they want to win, and being one of the few women in a male-dominated sport taught me how to be strategic -- _and not be intimidated._

I've learned to stay focused on what winning actually means: _delivering results._
* I've been a champion for efforts to improve street safety, increase affordable housing stock, and protect our climate;

* I led the effort to improve transparency and keep people safer from sexual harassment and retaliation in the state assembly;

* I banned toxic, cancer causing ingredients from personal care products, children’s clothing & toys, and mattress;

* I’ve even taken on online ticket sellers to ensure Californians can see their favorite performers without price-gouging.

[I'm in Congress because we need proven, effective leaders in Washington who have a track record of delivering results. In Washington, votes matter.
On the _[Deporting Fraudsters Act of 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/adccc022-f552-4e69-8080-4ab16b4ac54d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (H.R. 1958) _--a bill to ensure non-citizens who defraud American taxpayers can be deported--
Jim Himes voted **NO**.

### That's his record.

## **Fraud Has a Cost**
Americans lose **$50 -$100+ billion every year** to fraud and improper payments. and rhe Learing Center in Minneapolis was the tip of the iceberg.
That's money meant for:
* Seniors
* Veterans
* Working families

The question before Congress was simple:
**Should non-citizens who commit fraud face consequences?**
Jim Himes said: **No. - He said No to those who elected him who are subsidizing these frauds.**
## **This Was Not About Immigration -- It Was About Accountability**
This wasn't about:
* **DREAM** ers
* Visa overstays
* Pathways to citizenship

Those are real debates.
This vote was about one thing: **Fraud.**
## **Connecticut Families Already Pay the Price**
Connecticut leaders talk about budget shortfalls and affordability.
But reality is simple:
**If government spends more than it takes in, you either cut --or raise taxes.**
Families live that every day.
They should not have to **subsidize fraud, waste, and bad governance.**

Affordability starts with accountability.
That means:
* Enforcing the law
* Protecting taxpayer dollars
* Ending tolerance for fraud

subject: Big Wins for Rural Oregon
body:
The 2026 short session was filled with accomplishments for rural Oregon
---
| | | [](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fcontent.govdelivery.com%2Faccounts%2FORLEG%2Fbulletins%2F40f2745/1/0101019d094e0819-6bdd23c3-5c60-4b96-a5bd-e8c02e9a6c7b-000000/zStWIhLYeRSB23xjxQonH8L35ukjUF1IBsIgSQT6N-k=449)

---
# Big Wins for Rural Oregon
The 2026 session was short, but it was filled with wins for rural Oregon. I am honored to continue serving as your State Representative. My one goal is to champion protecting the rural way of life; and I am proud to have secured policy and budget victories for farmers, ranchers, and rural communities throughout Oregon.
## **The 2026 session was short, but it was filled with wins for rural Oregon.**
I am honored to continue serving as your State Representative. My one goal is to champion protecting the rural way of life; and I am proud to have secured policy and budget victories for farmers, ranchers, and rural communities throughout Oregon. Rep. Breese Iverson with the coalition of farmers supporting HB 4153
## Preserving pumpkin patches & family farms — HB 4153-A
In the final hours of the session, my bill, HB 4153-A, passed with strong bipartisan support. The vote was 40–14 in the House and 21–8 in the Senate. HB 4153-A is legislation to preserve family farm stores, like your favorite pumpkin patch and tulip farm. This bill creates a Farm Store permit to expand opportunities to sell local products, host seasonal agritourism events, such as corn mazes and flower festivals; and welcome families and educational opportunities for others experience life on the farm. It also has protections for farmland and provides counties clear, enforceable language for rules around important issues like public health and safety. Rep. Breese Iverson and Rep. Rieke Smith after passage of HB 4153 Farm Stores HB 4153-A is the result of strong collaboration from the Governor’s Office, Oregon Department of Agriculture, Oregon Farm Bureau, counties, and stakeholders representing farm operators across the state. Many hours were spent considering all aspects of this issue after my 2025 bill of similar intent did not make it across the finish line. There was support from across the state for getting clear direction and decision on this farm stores and I appreciate everyone who reached out. Passage of HB 4153-A is an important step to safeguard the future of Oregon agriculture, keep many established farm stores from closing and allow educational opportunities for those not raised on a farm. With this legislation, I am proud to highlight another aspect of how agriculture is Oregon’s foundation. Rep. Breese Iverson meeting with rural school district administrators
## Even more wins for Rural Oregon
More funding for county fairgrounds. I and other rural legislators have been pushing for years the necessity of our rural fairgrounds. These grounds are the heart of rural Oregon. The place where we gather for fairs, have important community events and stage emergency assistance in times of trouble. At the start of our next budget cycle (July 1, 2027) our county fairgrounds will start receiving a full 1% of lottery funds. Before this legislation, there has been a cap on funds flowing to fairgrounds. The cap is off and these funds will flow to all counties. These dollars will be much needed additional resources for repairs, upgrades and more. **Horse racing in Oregon.** I helped to secure $5 million for Crook, Harney, Josephine, Tillamook, and Union counties to ensure horse racing operations do not close. Preserving horse racing has been a priority for several years, and I am proud to deliver this for Crook County. **Terrebonne Wastewater project funding.** Without support from the state, the burden for a critical wastewater collection project in Terrebonne would fall solely on users after federal funding did not transpire. I am excited to report state funding of $2.4 million has been secured to assist this project! **Protecting Oregon Agriculture.** Over $2 million has been allocated to fight Japanese beetle and protect nursery market export access for Oregon nurseries. Nurseries are a top agriculture industry for Oregon; and without this program, many nurseries would have lost access to the import export markets. These dollars will help contain Japanese beetle where it is currently identified. **Closing the wolf compensation gap.** In the 2025, there was a push to create a solid stream of funding for wolf compensation in Oregon. The number of wolves continues to grow in our great state along with the number of wildlife and livestock killed by them. The 2025 bill did not pass but a similar bill passed this session. In addition to creating this new revenue stream, there was a funding gap left from the 2025-27 budget. This session $1 million was secured to close the budget gap for wolf compensation while the new funding stream gets set up and will continue into the future to compensate ranchers as a result of wolf deprivation. While these dollars are important to ranchers, now is the time for the U.S. Senate to do their part by removing wolves from the endangered species list! **Rebuilding Homes After Disasters — SB 1561**. It may not surprise you to learn when a home is destroyed in a fire or other natural disaster, there is significant government red tape to prevent rebuilding. SB 1561 fixes many of those issues. There is more to be done when we lose homes and communities to devastating wildfires, but this bill is a step in the right direction. **Tax relief for on farm processing operations — HB 4130**. This bill will allow farmers to obtain special assessment for land underneath buildings being used for preparation or processing of farm products. HB 4130 resolves decades old confusion about whether a farmer is “preparing” farm products for market, or “processing” products into value-added goods. Additionally, the bill also grants farmers who are processing their products, property tax relief if at least 25% of the goods they are processing come from their own farm. HB 4130 is another win for agriculture in Oregon as it allows farmers to vertically integrate without risk of a crushing tax bill. **Key budget items protected.** During the early part of the budget process, FFA, outdoor school programs, and extension programs were all at risk of being cut. Thanks to many of you, Legislators received overwhelming response to these proposed cuts in the form of emails and phone calls - your advocacy was the key to protecting this funding! **Wildfire and Rural Infrastructure.** While dollars were tight this short session, it is imperative dollars secured in previous budgets remained secure and were delivered where needed most. I worked with agencies and colleagues to make sure dollars were not cut from programs just getting started, additional dollars were included in a few areas to support previous efforts and transparency highlighted for these dollars. Vice Chair Breese Iverson running House Housing Committee
## Continuing to tackle Oregon’s Housing Crisis
Housing affordability and availability remain front and center in Oregon. While our work is far from over, several bipartisan housing bills advanced this session to make meaningful progress: **One-time UGB expansion fixes — HB 4035.** SB 1537 (2024) created a one-time opportunity for cities to expand their UGB for housing. We made several important fixes to ensure this limited expansion will work better for more cities who want to use it. **Housing Omnibus — HB 4037.** The omnibus housing bill this session is really about technical and language fixes for issues and programs passed in previous legislative sessions such as revolving loan funds, city and county building department review processes. **Housing opportunities for those 55 years and older — HB 4082.** Authorizes a one-time urban growth boundary (UGB) expansion using the same process created in SB 1537 (2024) for up to 100 acres for larger cities or 50 acres for smaller ones to develop housing prioritized for Oregonians 55 and older. **Allowing a change in smoking policies for rentals — HB 4120.** We passed new legislation to landlords to prohibit smoking in residential rentals, protecting tenants’ health and safety. Rep. Breese Iverson meets with Regional Business Alliance
## Fighting for your rights... and your wallet
**Delaying Measure 114 — HB 4145-B.** For the past several sessions, Democrats have sought to override the courts to implement an adjusted gun control scheme based on Measure 114. Republicans were able to block many horrible provisions in this bill by working together and negotiating new language in the waining days of session. HB 4145-B delays the implementation to January 1, 2028, to provide more time for rulings from the Oregon Supreme Court and federal courts. This is great news for those of us who own firearms. **Stopped attempts to steal your Kicker — HB 4125 & SJR 201.** Despite being enshrined in Oregon State Constitution, Salem Democrats always want to find new revenue for Oregon’s budget by stealing or redistributing your Kicker. As a member of key budget committees, I fight wasteful spending of millions of your tax dollars. The Kicker is off the table as far as I am concerned. Any tax money we can return to you, is money well spent in my view. **Preventing even higher insurance premiums — HB 4098 & SB 1517.** This session I believe we struck the right balance on trying to make insurance more affordable. We stopped a bill to make all kinds of insurance more expensive (HB 4098) and reformed recreation liability to ensure continued access to all the loved outdoor activities Oregonians love and tourists visit to enjoy! With insurance premiums already far too high, stopping HB 4098 was imperative. Getting SB 1517 over the finish line preserves many of our recreational opportunities from skiing to bounce houses! **“Disconnecting” from federal tax code — SB 1507.** I opposed this legislation because I believe 100% of the federal tax benefits should apply to your state taxes. When affordability is a top issue for Oregonians, the focus should be about how to make living in Oregon work for families. SB 1507 picks and chooses which pieces of the federal tax code Oregonians will align with and which pieces where Oregon will keep more tax dollars. While SB 1507 could have been much worse, it does preserve some key aspects of the One Big Beautiful Bill such as no tax on tips and no tax on overtime. **We missed out on JOBS Act — SB 1586.** I was a chief sponsor of SB 1586 because I believe Oregon needs shout from the mountain tops to the rest of the nation and world-wide, we are ‘Open for Business’. SB 1586 would help us remain competitive in the semiconductor industry, advanced manufacturing, expanded the R&D tax credit to make Oregon competitive for new industries, and strengthened the enterprise zone program to allow rural Oregon to compete for jobs. We need the real living wage jobs this legislation would have promoted. I am disappointed it did not pass. **Governor’s Prosperity Bill — HB 4084.** I supported the Governor’s bill to speed up permitting in specific limited cases, fund site readiness for industrial projects, and improve Oregon’s enterprise zone program. While this bill has pieces I do not align with, the good of this bill is worth supporting and extra sideboards are limited in duration.
## Elections
**Campaign finance limits — HB 4018.** Clarifies contribution limits which become effective January 1, 2027, and delays many of the complex parts of the law to 2033. Hopefully this delay will provide time to fix the complexity, give those implementing it time to build the systems, along with tweaking the language again to give voters’ the real transparency they thought they were getting with their initial vote. **Moving the gas tax election to May — SB 1599.** I opposed SB 1599 because this was more about politics then doing the will of the voters. The original referendum signed by 250,000 petitioners specified a November vote. Legislators found a way to fill the gap in ODOT funding for this year and this referendum should have been left alone.
## Looking Ahead
This short session reinforced an important truth: Oregon’s success depends on balance and respect for the views and way of life in rural Oregon. I will continue to fight for local control, protecting farming and ranching, opposing new and higher taxes, and keeping government accountable. Thank you to all who reached out during this session. Please know all the emails and phone calls were received and discussed with my team! I have an amazing team who helps wade through the chaos of session. I am truly blessed by my team and the ability to continue to serve you. If you have questions or want to share your thoughts on session outcomes, please reach out to my office. Your voice matters—and it truly shapes the work we do in Salem. Sincerely, Vikki Breese Iverson

name: Unite4Freedom
subject: We Won In Court!
body:
An 8th Circuit federal judge ordered Missouri to follow federal election law.
|
---
Dear Peter, An 8th Circuit federal judge ordered Missouri to follow federal election law. The judge ruled that the state can’t block a citizen from using the federal election complaint process due to arbitrary state rules, after the state dismissed her complaint without a hearing. Connie, a Unite4Freedom volunteer, courageously filed a Help America Vote Act (HAVA) complaint with the state of Missouri alleging issues with the statewide voter registration database and whether it complies with federal law. The state tried to shut her down, but she didn’t take “no” for an answer.
---
| [ **Read Press Release** ](https://d56tDQ04.na1.hubspotlinks.com/Ctc/UD+113/d56tDQ04/VW498-8tPC5_W8CZrRg6hxL47W7nzmJr5LTq81MGxfSR5kBVzW50kH_H6lZ3q2W6G-4hB62ZwlQW82drjq7T1vd3W7D5Q23801pRpW1y9GH38hYFBHW46tl8J4_rYTJW90wL4N77bGBLN8cJZhGm_f10W4JSRPn2F26slW74Q7_-77kLQ8W3Tm7T53_r0gYW5Tqb7V16990bW7rwsBz6MZ3GjW3MWV_16Px90tW4Clvhn7z61yqW8XP86F3WW8fQW4JZCTZ1FSrglW1t_5Dr8R2mV_W4BXPln7VLPHWW95Nv6t34Kr8-W1mPMdw1gRQkcW2xGs2N1vBF3HW1kCMv0528V0LW3hNsl43tBHXJW7xdpQ85p7Ff4W2r7HjR8-Mkn9W7czfk744tLRqW7VNXr92llXFDN8dXM-HxkBymW5fDCZh7F2TwKW6WZ5BL9bry_jMQzL1SdxdWTW9dbVDm6yCwxFf4FB2v-04)
---
For years, states have avoided these hearings using technicalities. But a federal court confirmed that the state MAY NOT block a citizen’s federal rights and MUST give Connie the hearing she requested. The federal judge is so concerned that he didn’t just rule in her favor and pass it back to the state. ## Pentagon Seeks $200B for Iran War
The Pentagon is [asking Congress for roughly $200 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O6yAUQOHV4M7R5ULsuKB4jbu8dkoLw-VnhMEyJJ7sfpRsYeojfcX5ui93HVPM_r_eSDVXlkxnTdQaHcupD_fINmbf9E81eqs6Wx1PWhBw6EH0CIvVMb0W2VnliJBER4qPowTgUoouKHkbVq6dQEerQynHYTIGBjLSCLRm7aJ6ayAQOHCQ_HKd7GTgBg60tvI6MAlkYyvH5bvE3AK59CpPOi6mbF1SobW9MvGP4cxwboFCTOndGM57SdG8GM6WHOVKDOfrOHEcb30g76mF_lNs7XfKTfuS-_VhPTWGc3cou58xpViHkUnwm44fuGt_OvVU-BsAAP__Mc59Sg) to fund the war in Iran and restock its weapons supply. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth confirmed the request Thursday, telling reporters, _"Obviously it takes money to kill bad guys,"_ as the U.S. has now [struck more than 7,000 targets](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u2zAQhE8jdRSWP5KfChZp3DltSmFNLuVNKNIgGdO-faBc4XUDDDCD7_t1227IkdP-Ew-yLeQtUa-RWqOydSzhb_Kc9obv6vComDxyp02BWgRooWDzyPGzmdHbQKRIj2Tl5WIApDF6fFgf1nAPLkgNC85hhrv6WtE5GcBrPcuR7bkGWoEECUZO8-pXB18QANGbeRkMkOeWy_Q7c2oPCvGTX1Qml48x2kdrzzroH4O6Durae59Cfp8UZz-o6zNHbuzqGSk13HMSlehPFZGwNqEA7iKUfAiX016oVsEFk-hYxmL9s3OMXJfLYGA_kOP_2_YtVy-r_gUAAP__K9t_zw) and sunk dozens of Iranian vessels since the conflict began Feb. 28. The war's economic toll deepened Wednesday after Iran launched [retaliatory strikes on energy facilities](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkM2q2zAQRp9G3inoz3G88KJQDF3cbrs0Y2nkTFGky2h807x9SV-h6w8-zjm_PrYPoEL1-AkPXCS3reKzFxRB3p7A-ayJ6iHwp0d4dKgJ6ImbM-6qjdfObAmovLYwpCUjOvQDLnaagjE2BD_cl3HC_Tb6-Zb9HjPauMPVzrfgZpjMbueBlveb8c5YY02wl3FOczQ3kw1ACuNVBYOJpPHld6Mqd8zl1b6QL7E9hrLcRT678t-UW5VbYY9vg_em3PqjCnIFoVahKLcSQ9UCfKB0fZwl69jOKkzYNVbk46WpZoYufEY5GTVkQdbUGbCQcmuXxi_lV0rKf7fe2nkagx14SZ9PKoX6dVLBHA-g8o9P_ivq1-L-BgAA__88jo1m) in Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates, hitting the world's largest liquefied natural gas terminal and sending global oil prices surging. Meanwhile, Iran's regime [hanged 19-year-old champion wrestler](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DmO3DAUBNDTUBkbn0trCRg4UTZOHQpf4meLBheB5LRatzfkK0xcwENV_flavtAHn16_MZJpLi-JzhqoNSrLicV9J-vTq-GnbhgrJov-pEWC7DkoLmGx6MO16M4aRyRJdWTEMGgAobXqdkNuVGKQK6xqgH4dexwABrGtT6dGh6Lz5tZASRAgQIvHc7LTBiM4QLT62TMNZH3L5fE3-9R2cuHKbyqPLccumL21ozL1i8mZyTldR67tjpicb5jJGRSTs5iYnM9cguX3RCZnXzBx-tD23ahyMfGLsPAcLN92jIfPiZ-FagtUeMVAO495xxjRet7OzHPbqdxQV4w9Th-Cr_3ANLwi-vC_XfvRpW8j_wUAAP__5SOKpQ) Saleh Mohammadi and two other men for protesting against the government, ignoring pleas from the U.S. State Department and sparking calls for an international sports boycott.
## Historic Heat Wave Bakes the West

## Corpus Christi Gets Some Water Relief

## Study Shows Dallas Summers Are Getting Hotter
The number of 100-degree days in Dallas and Fort Worth [has climbed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLvO4yAUhJ8Gd1jHXHwpKLZx92-7pUXgOCBBiOA4Tt5-5bzC34000jf65t_P9mNjio_7X5vR0Hsv2wPPlpAI6-ZKfR7NhRobxdMS1oop4n7bBIiRg-QCNm9j-myq8-YGfhk6NMM0KQClRuiCASGGHeZRo3T7BLh4oWe1aLdov88zdtFcMJAChgFA695rsHpElPrmhFw8U4A-Uqk9BSR827anT3lh7V3JXTKB6NmY_MPEysR6nmf_saGUq2VivXSYWG2l6BJeMR8u8FAuQ_7F8XbkjLVxd9RYjsYHCQCgZ90Hyqmrxj_PmFJs48QU3LON6btNv3vsZcT_AAAA__-Yl4DU) in recent decades, according to a study by the _Dallas Morning News_. By averaging the number of triple-digit days each year per decade, the report found that the 2020s have been the hottest period so far, just edging out the 1950s. | Friend,
We have a troubling update about Democrats' first major election of the year.
New polling in the April 7 Wisconsin Supreme Court election shows this race on a knife's edge. Judge Chris Taylor leads by just 5 points and 66% of voters are still undecided.
That means this election is a dead heat and could swing either way. And if our voters don't turn out, MAGA could seize this crucial Supreme Court seat.

---
| [](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Lyy1lHhRQBU41r17vRQzOejWCVePYFaJaPQ5d4JOdhccDDKJ2kP5NFlB780FkrteG0LNTsEf2MOnxcjO3rZR8MiKNZq3yqSvZIeYfLRCh3siHFtEh_vFVx-Q6E0c7luyFn4c51hn4MBVIguRCcyePS9rlvgcPfJW7nmR7kdWe0myl5nmWUtl4uwr3_TGpo8lSAfrTCh2wwpc4BbJgLhFLpwbY1GGxJq22zgOt4JyeeFSe8YMjZxHwKLzg-ouvpYSYYbe6BgZ-gY=&c=Vw5_pMGQE7v9XAQBiMJynoZu_dtr_l0OJUtCVBcLmeMwrCzcKT0Uag==&ch=C9eIgJGkE6oruamDNlI8X0gtIryRl0auhlX4CLx3hGwBDMSYaFkGsQ==)
---
| If MAGA candidate Maria Lazar wins, a critical firewall protecting free and fair elections could disintegrate into dust in August 2028, just months before the next presidential election.
If we lose this court, the consequences would be dire for Dems:
---
* The same court that blocked Trump's election schemes in 2020 could fall into extremist hands
* National momentum could shift toward MAGA just before the midterms
* Wisconsinites could face attacks on fundamental rights -- including reproductive freedom

---
| And here's the most alarming number of all to come out that poll:
55% of Wisconsin voters say they've heard little about this race. 38% say they've heard nothing.
Volatile polling like this is exactly the opening MAGA billionaires look for. If they flood the race with cash in these closing months, they could pull off a coup.

| | A few days ago, a man pulled me aside at a house party after my talk and the Q&A. He admitted, “I came into this room a pessimist. I’m leaving thinking you may be one of the few people who could beat Tim Burchett." I’m running to flip a congressional seat that hasn’t changed party hands since 1867. That's no small feat, and you deserve to know a little bit about me – and why I think winning this race is possible.

Y’all might already know that I’m a scientist (I have a PhD in Civil Engineering), and a small business owner (I own KnoxFill in South Knox), and that I spent a year working inside Congress as a Science Policy Fellow. Some things you might not know: ➡️ I grew up on a horse farm as the youngest of four daughters in a staunchly Republican family (I’m sure there are pictures of me at Bush Cheney rallies as a kid). ➡️ I’ve had a lot of jobs: nanny, magazine editor, farmhand, server, Spanish teacher, trip leader, research and teaching assistant, and business owner. I know what it’s like to worry about making payroll – and wonder why the amount on your check is so much lower than you thought it would be after working so hard at an hourly, tipped job. ➡️ My husband Max and I met in Knoxville while he was getting his PhD at UT in Energy Sciences. He recently became a U.S. citizen. I’m so proud of him and grateful he’s a citizen of the country we both love so much. **So why do I actually think we can win this?** **_We are building a movement to meet this moment._** When we host events, it's not just engaged, establishment Democrats showing up. It's Independents, former Republicans, young people, and people who've felt politically lost or politically hopeless for years.

We're building this campaign from the ground up. Hiring locally, growing political power and infrastructure here instead of sending all of our money to out-of-state consultants, creating the kind of community infrastructure that actually lasts beyond Election Day. As of this week, we have 500+ volunteers [(join us!)](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/--jxi1M6BOZWMBysQQd6Ww~~/AAUS1hA~/P05l86pbp18HtCS0Rxy-J3sAJVlT9Ugfx7WC47eAhfzJ6gu3ZSFTy0AI_laJfaMTdFj8IX3a33s3QcnlCmgtxZrAcUV83NANSTD4hlWUldj4OMn5u3UPAr-cP1dsQH04a_JmXYCu7zugyrYO9fSZFjTPjwm2Da1YTkvvdpAZYtElO2401p0SVd8B5-9ilACbA-4eb60ET4spYqkhqNzfig~~) ready to knock doors, make phone calls, hold events, and flip this district.

I know the odds we're up against. But TN-02 deserves a representative who will never sell this district out for a handshake and a photo op.

We can do this. **But only with you.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. body:
#

Peter,
It feels like every day, the depravity deepens and the chaos accelerates.
The President and his family are raking in billions while Americans struggle to make ends meet.
Millions are losing health insurance. Rural hospitals are shutting down services. Meanwhile, billionaires get another round of tax cuts.
More and more of our neighbors carry their passports to the store in case they're detained based on their accent or the color of their skin.
And now our country is plunged into a regime-change war-of-choice without evidence of an imminent threat, without clear objectives, without a plan for the aftermath, and without the consent of Congress.
Maybe you fear whether our Republic now, in our 250th year, can survive it all.
I believe it can. _I believe we will overcome this — all of this — together._
Because across this country, people of every background and belief are rejecting the chaos and corruption. And I'm fighting every day to hold this administration accountable and make sure the people of Georgia are served with decency by their government.
But this is exactly why Trump and his MAGA billionaire allies are coming after my Senate seat with everything they've got.
In these 2026 midterms, I'm the only Democratic U.S. Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won. The Administration knows Democrats could retake the Senate, and they know a Republican winning here in Georgia would make that nearly impossible. _They know this is the most crucial Senate race in the country._
[**So you’re furious about what’s happening to our country, and ready to fight back, please chip in to support our campaign here in Georgia:**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-mar26.B6mAX1&refcode=em260320-1-f&t=1&akid=1901%2E5691347%2EGUQEdI)

Trump and his loyalists are the cruelest and most arrogant people ever to occupy high office in the modern history of the United States. They are the most corrupt clique of grifters and sycophants ever to run our country. And their cruelty, arrogance, and corruption are matched only by their incompetence.
Remember when Trump promised prices would come down on day one?
Instead, his tariffs are driving prices higher and higher.
American manufacturing jobs have declined every month since those "Liberation Day" tariffs began.
And last year more jobs were lost than any year since COVID.
Trump promised to fight for the working class. Instead, rural clinics and hospitals are getting defunded so the wealthiest people can get another tax cut.
_But it doesn't have to be this way._
We can pull our country out of this moral tailspin and recommit ourselves to the values that have sustained this nation for nearly 250 years.
But none of that happens unless we win this November, and the battle in Georgia is already underway.
I need you. Georgia needs you. Our country needs you.

#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260320-1-b&t=1&akid=11312%2E3935704%2EsbNkRc)
---
Hello, it's Gabby Giffords.
When Mark and I were making a decision about whether we’d start an organization focused on gun violence prevention, we knew the challenges we would face.
Many people in Washington D.C. said it would be political poison to stand up against the gun lobby. The NRA had millions of dollars at their disposal — and they would use every cent to drown us out. It wasn’t going to be easy.
But after the tragic shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School, which stole 20 innocent children’s lives and six staff members, we knew that doing nothing wasn’t an option.
So, we founded what is now known as GIFFORDS. And after more than a decade of hard work, we’ve made gun safety a winning issue. We’ve passed hundreds of gun safety laws across the nation and the NRA is in the weakest position it’s ever been.
I am so grateful every single day to do this work. I have never forgotten the fights we’ve taken on and won together. The amount of lives we’ve helped save — this is all because of grassroots supporters like you.
Now, we face an inflection point. As I write this, President Trump’s administration is working to roll back our progress on gun safety. They are putting all of their weight towards flooding our streets with more guns and helping their gun lobby allies profit.
I know that we have what it takes to end the gun violence epidemic in our country. But I cannot do it alone.
**[Can you please make a donation to support GIFFORDS PAC before the clock strikes midnight? March is a make-or-break month for us, and we cannot afford to fall behind.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260320-1-b&t=2&akid=11312%2E3935704%2EsbNkRc)

Gabby Giffords

If you want Lina Khan back the best think you can do is support AGs who are actually in the fight today, and those who might lead the fight tomorrow against monopoly power and corruption.
| | | [_David Seligman_](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/486d56ba?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21) is one of my favorite candidates in the countryHe's running for Colorado Attorney General with absolutely no fear of criticizing the Democratic Party when they sell working people out. (By name, like Governor Polis). Last weekend, in the first real vote of the 2026 Democratic primary, he came out on top. 38% to 36% over the perceived frontrunner, in a straw poll of delegates elected at caucuses held across Colorado by actual Democratic voters.Before we get to the race, let's talk about why this job matters more right now than it ever has.Our federal enforcers, including the Department of Justice's Antitrust Division are being systematically corrupted by the Trump administration. Trump settled with Ticketmaster and is pretending the Paramount deal is legal when it looks like part of a corrupt deal to get Trump to control CNN content. State attorneys general are sometimes an afterthought in the fight against monopoly power, but they are actually the key, the whole ballgame right now: Bonta says he's investigating Paramount, and it's the states that are still litigating Ticketmaster, determined to break up their illegal monopolization efforts. It'll be the states that will have to lead in taking on BigTech and private equity and the concentrations of wealth and power that are destroying the country. It is critical to have state AGs who are imaginative, serious, and driven by a desire for fairness to stop rampant white collar illegality. That's Seligman. It's not just that he has good politics. He's been doing the work for years, standing up in court on behalf of working people-building the bold, imaginative legal theories to take on the largest corporate landlord in America for [_illegally overcharging tenants_](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/93ba48d2?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21), the meatpacker [_JBS for systematically injuring workers_](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/13d20f52?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)on the line and treating them as disposable, [_Uber and Lyft_](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/1c222d96?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)for using algorithms to control their drivers while also cheating them out of pay. And when Colorado's own Democratic Governor tried to cooperate with ICE to hand over the private information of immigrant workers -- without a court order, in violation of state law -- Seligman didn't stay quiet. He and his team helped [_bring the lawsuit to stop him_](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/5986f434?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21), while he was running for attorney general. This is not a politician who discovered that working people exist six months before an election. He has spent his entire career in the courtroom and in state legislatures across the country fighting for people who couldn't fight back alone.His most prominent opponent in this race is Jena Griswold, Colorado's current Secretary of State. She's better known, better funded, and has spent months telling anyone who will listen that she's the inevitable frontrunner, which is clearly not true. This race is massively important, for Colorado, and for people across the country. Seligman can pull off the upset here. We see that now. But especially as he gains more ground, corporate interests are going to pay even more attention to this race -- including corporate interests that he's taken on directly. [_We have to get him as much help as we can_](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/eeb941ca?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21) _._ If you support him, I promise you you'll feel a part of enormous pride when he brings the most innovative, aggressive, serious antitrust cases in the country. Want Lina Khan back? Support incredible candidates for AG.Hope you're well and I've got some more soon,
Zephyr Teachout

This time a year ago, Donald Trump promised Americans $2,000 rebate checks, and that all of our bills would be cut in half.
He promised that DOGE would cut trillions of dollars of waste from the federal budget and that there would be no new wars.
Now look where we are. Higher grocery and gas prices, way higher housing costs, spiking energy bills, and out-of-reach health care costs. A vulnerable economy with higher unemployment. And a new war in Iran without a plan or end in sight.
And yet, Donald Trump brags about how proud he is of this economy.
That’s a stunning thing to think, let alone say out loud!
Might as well be Marie Antoinette declaring, let them eat cake .
This economy may be working just fine for the 1% or the billionaires but it is not working for everyday people.
When I travel across Virginia and talk to people, no one tells me the economy is “roaring.” They want their leaders to be focused on helping them afford their lives, not distracted by vanity projects, personal grudges, and rewriting history.
Trump can keep pretending everything is great, but the rest of us know better.
Trump promised to lower costs on Day One, but his reckless economic policies have driven prices up for everyone. And new data shows that American households paid an average of $1,000 more over the past year thanks to Trump’s idiotic and pointless tariffs.
I’ve been battling Trump’s tariff idiocy in the Senate since he got back into office, and I’m proud that both Congress and the Supreme Court have taken a stand and rolled back some of his worst tariff policies.
But Trump has shown he’s not done gaslighting hardworking Americans and enriching himself and his buddies, so I’m continuing to fight to give families some actual relief.
I need your voice in this fight — will you add your name today to stand with me against Trump’s failed economic policies and reckless tariffs? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/6OlBvusaiE2tf2hTD4s3LA2]

We can lower costs, protect working families, and hold this administration accountable — but only if we stand together.
