Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. Hi friend, Between getting petition signatures and holding events across the district, Team Wallace has been hard at work this past month. Read on for some campaign updates and how you can be part of the movement we’re building together. **What We’ve Been Up To** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127745674/609060655/-653362279?refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.03.20_b1_ktrwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQxM2NhMWMtYTQyNC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hOf4ymU3GPjhc5jEcdgCsIiJiC34KLKPYo04I4z662s=)
* **Getting Rachel on the ballot (!).** Thanks to the incredible work of so many this petition season, our campaign rivaled Dan Meuser, filing nearly 4,000 signatures. **And it’s official: Rachel will be the only Democrat on the ballot this May. Over the course of three weeks, she and our campaign team went to 35 events in all 12 counties.** We outworked an incumbent congressman in a district where registered Republicans outnumber Democrats. In a district where Democrats have been counted out for years, we’re showing what’s possible when we roll up our sleeves and get to work. And this is just the beginning. Being the presumptive Democratic nominee means we get to turn our focus to the real task ahead: Beating Dan Meuser – and we need all hands on deck to do that in November. [**SIGN UP NOW to join our volunteer kick-off call next week!** (more on this below).](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127745676/609060657/634841355?refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.03.20_b1_ktrwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQxM2NhMWMtYTQyNC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hOf4ymU3GPjhc5jEcdgCsIiJiC34KLKPYo04I4z662s=&emci=ad640dd5-8824-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=1d13ca1c-a424-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=18681717)
* **Holding Dan Meuser accountable.** ICYMI, Dan Meuser wants to help ICE and the federal government bring in a 7,500-person mega facility. [Even though the local roads can’t handle the 150 trucks a day that would be required to remove sewage from the complex, there already isn’t enough water in the ground for the people who live in Tremont, and no local police force and just one ambulance service, which would have to take on an estimated 16 to 32 EMS calls for the 7,500 people.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127745678/609060659/1478927316?refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.03.20_b1_ktrwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQxM2NhMWMtYTQyNC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hOf4ymU3GPjhc5jEcdgCsIiJiC34KLKPYo04I4z662s=&emci=ad640dd5-8824-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=1d13ca1c-a424-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=18681717) I talked with Joyce, the owner of Kids-R-Kids Child Care Center, at a town hall last Friday. She told me the ICE facility will be the end of her business – parents are already saying they’ll pull their kids out if this facility goes forward. She reached out to Meuser for help. He never got back to her.
* **Building momentum on the ground.** From celebrating St. Patrick’s Day in the [Pottsville Parade](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127745679/609060660/348051648?refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.03.20_b1_ktrwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQxM2NhMWMtYTQyNC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hOf4ymU3GPjhc5jEcdgCsIiJiC34KLKPYo04I4z662s=&emci=ad640dd5-8824-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=1d13ca1c-a424-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=18681717) and [Berks County](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127745681/609060662/-139033448?refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.03.20_b1_ktrwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQxM2NhMWMtYTQyNC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hOf4ymU3GPjhc5jEcdgCsIiJiC34KLKPYo04I4z662s=&emci=ad640dd5-8824-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=1d13ca1c-a424-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=18681717), to [a roundtable in Athens](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127745683/609060664/-385426048?refcode=b26_em_msg_2026.03.20_b1_ktrwfc_newsletter&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQxM2NhMWMtYTQyNC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hOf4ymU3GPjhc5jEcdgCsIiJiC34KLKPYo04I4z662s=&emci=ad640dd5-8824-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=1d13ca1c-a424-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=18681717) to discuss how important it is for local communities to feel in control of their destiny, we’re growing this movement by connecting with people where they are.

Dear Valued Subscriber and Movie & Music Lovers,
Oh, what a triumph of artistic integrity! The iHeart Awards 2026, hosted by Ludacris--a man who definitely hasn't spent two decades perfecting the art of radio-friendly controversy--has blessed us with a nominee list that reads like a "Greatest Hits of Questionable Decision Making." Earlier in his career, he faced criticism from local authorities regarding his lyrics, the use of the N-word, and his representation of women.
In early 2026, he faced backlash and withdrew from the "Rock the Country" festival, a 2026 tour headlined by Kid Rock, due to the event's "**[MAGA-coded](https://substack.com/redirect/9542d43a-d040-4e7d-8c39-31e4833be8fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** ," pro-Trump, and conservative associations. Social media critics heavily criticized Ludacris for participating in a "MAGA-linked" event, according to **[Rolling Stone](https://substack.com/redirect/3470d39e-c9fb-4f3b-a8c7-23f26795ff15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[Independent Mail](https://substack.com/redirect/949fff25-9d60-482c-a05f-adfb2994ed18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
Nothing screams "wholesome entertainment" quite like gathering Kendrick Lamar, Taylor Swift, Bad Bunny, Cardi B, and Justin Bieber under one roof to celebrate John Mellencamp with an Icon Award. Because if there's one thing the youth need, it's another boomer rock star getting a participation trophy while his musical grandchildren collect nominations despite their, shall we say, _colorful_ relationship with controversy. John Mellencamp is so fed up with rowdy fans at his shows **[he stormed off the stage](https://substack.com/redirect/d30a0420-03ec-4e77-96cd-90bfa5925fba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during a recent performance.
How refreshing that the committee scoured the industry to highlight artists with "sick, dark backgrounds"--because why reward consistent talent when you can celebrate drama, legal troubles, and public meltdowns? It's not like there are thousands of hardworking musicians who haven't assaulted anyone, broken laws, or tormented their exes online. But sure, let's give Cardi B another platform and act surprised when the ceremony turns into a therapy session disguised as entertainment.
Truly, iHeart has its finger on the pulse of what matters: marketing potential over morality, headlines over harmony. Can't wait for next year's "Problematic Behavior" category!
That's why we created the Heartland AwardsTM. To support and celebrate the performers and artists with heart.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: 23 years after the invasion of Iraq, Donald Trump is dragging us into another war in the Middle East
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
If we want to avoid the same mistakes we made 23 years ago today, we cannot sit by and do nothing while this war unfolds.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260320-6031-footer&t=1&akid=6031%2E420207%2Exik1tC)
Peter,
Today marks 23 years since the US invaded Iraq. What followed was a war that led to widespread civilian suffering—hundreds of thousands killed, injured, or displaced—and the deaths of more than 4,400 U.S. soldiers.
After the 9/11 attacks, a wave of anti-Muslim and anti-immigrant sentiment swept across the country. I couldn’t sit by while Americans were targeted based on their culture or where they were born. So I started Hate Free Zone, which is now called OneAmerica, so that immigrants and refugees had a place to organize together and create a future where they could thrive. I continue that fight today, standing up and fighting for justice at the national level.
**Now, 23 years later, we find ourselves under another Republican administration dragging us into another new war in the Middle East, and stoking more anti-immigrant and anti-Muslim sentiment. And I won’t stand for it.**
While Congress approved the war in Iraq, Trump hasn’t even asked for Congress’ approval for his war in Iran. It’s illegal, unconstitutional, and has already led to the deaths of 13 US service members and the injury of hundreds more.
And just like Iraq, it has the potential to unleash a wave of instability across the region, with far-reaching consequences that will be left for another president and another generation to deal with.
If we want to avoid the same mistakes we made 23 years ago today, we cannot sit by and do nothing while this war unfolds. We’ve seen Donald Trump bend to public pressure before — if enough of us speak out, we can build the pressure it will take to force him to end this war before it’s too late.
[**That’s why I’m asking you to sign on to my petition demanding Trump end his illegal war in Iran.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/em20260320-iran-war-petition/?source=em20260320-6031&t=2&akid=6031%2E420207%2Exik1tC)
**[Add Your Name](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/em20260320-iran-war-petition?source=em20260320-6031&t=3&akid=6031%2E420207%2Exik1tC)**
In the early 2000s, too many of those who opposed the war on terror stayed silent for fear of being branded “unpatriotic” or “traitor.” That silence is what allowed those wars to continue. We cannot stay silent this time.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

I hope you are too. As usual, the campaign team has been on the road every day, bringing our message of permanent affordability to every corner of Wisconsin. Everywhere I travel, I'm struck by how much we all have in common. The rent is too high. The wages are too low. The system isn't working for working people. And whether you're in Marinette or Milwaukee, people want the same thing: a governor who actually gets it. This is what gives me hope — even in places where you wouldn't expect to find many people who agree with me, real conversations are happening. People are listening. And they're hungry for something different. Peter, I have a confession to make. Peter, I want to take a moment to say thank you.

On Tuesday night, I called Lieutenant Governor Juliana Stratton and congratulated her on winning this primary. I trust that she will continue the lasting legacy that Senator Durbin leaves behind and offer her my full support on the road ahead.

This isn’t the result we’d hoped for, but I am still filled with immense gratitude.

I’m proud of the race we ran, and I’m honored by the support we received in every corner of this state.

# [#]

Most of all, I’m grateful to folks like you, who have stood with me every step of the way. I’m grateful for every person who knocked doors, talked to their neighbors, and the nearly 90,000 grassroots donors who powered this campaign.

This campaign may be over, but my gratitude and friendship will be forever.

I want to leave you with this:

Only in America can an immigrant kid with twenty-nine letters in his name go from living in public housing and relying on food stamps to serving in the halls of Congress.

But right now, those ideals are under threat like never before.

No matter what, I will continue to fight for our country, the greatest on Earth, to make the United States of America the kind of country we all still believe in.

I’m not giving up that fight, and I know you won’t either, Peter.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

body:
Working families are getting squeezed.

| |
---
Team, Donald Trump slapped tariffs on everything, promised it would make your life cheaper, and then watched 92,000 jobs disappear last month. So I've got a name for that: Trump's Broken Promise Economy. Gas prices are up. Heating costs are up. Groceries, the rent, the prescription drugs — all up. Companies are passing every single tariff cost straight to you, while Trump calls it a win. For years, Democrats have been paralyzed trying to figure out how to respond to this. I'm not. Here's what's actually happening in Massachusetts right now: — Rent is too high.
— Childcare is out of reach.
— Drug prices are still crushing families.
— And the ultra-wealthy? Still not paying their fair share. This isn't some economic inevitability. It's the direct result of Donald Trump's choices. And someone needs to say it plainly and fight back. That's why I'm running. We need to build more housing, lower drug prices, expand job training, and make the wealthy pay what they owe, so working families can actually get ahead. **[If you're ready for a Democrat who knows how to fight back, chip in $20 today and help us build a campaign that punches back for Massachusetts families.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127748154/609067421/2090747700?refcode=260320_sm_afford_b1&amount=20&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMWY1YWQxNy1hYjI0LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=WKmr21Aemyr_B-jH9MjFvxomK3VDSTmzkcCjCW9XaHM=)** | [CHIP IN $20](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127748155/609067422/1375639745?refcode=260320_sm_afford_b1&amount=20&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMWY1YWQxNy1hYjI0LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=WKmr21Aemyr_B-jH9MjFvxomK3VDSTmzkcCjCW9XaHM=)

U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.), a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, accepted the 2026 Hometown Hero award from the Alabama League of Municipalities (ALM). This award honors Senator Britt for her commitment to strengthening communities and improving the quality of life for local residents.

“Each and every day in the U.S. Senate, I’m fighting hard for our values, our people, and our state,” Britt said. “Nothing is more important to me than growing opportunity in Alabama, and I am so fortunate to have such outstanding state partners who share this goal and actively communicate the needs and priorities of their communities.

President Donald Trump was joined by Alabama U.S. Senators Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) and Tommy Tuberville (R-Auburn), along with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs General John D. Caine, and U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson at Dover Air Force Base this week for the dignified transfer of six American servicemembers killed during Operation Epic Fury — including three from Alabama.

Among those honored was Major Alex Klinner, 33, of Trussville — an Auburn University graduate and eight-year Air Force veteran who flew 362 combat hours and 181 combat support hours across four deployments. He is survived by his wife, Libby, and three young children.

“Attending the dignified transfer of Maj. Alex Klinner today was humbling and heartbreaking. In recent days, I’ve learned more about Maj. Klinner—the many lives he touched, the devoted family man he was, and his deep love of country,” Senator Britt said on Wednesdsay.

body:
[ stdin# ][IMG]

Hi Patrick, this email’s going to be a little longer because I want to make sure you know who I am and why I’m running. And yes, I am going to ask you for your support at the end, so if you’re short on time, you can click here to pitch in now.

My story started in the heart of Milwaukee in the 53206 zip code, Wisconsin’s poorest and the nation’s most incarcerated.

Baby Mandela Barnes

My grandfather moved to Milwaukee after serving during World War II. He worked in a factory, and there were thousands of people just like him whose jobs paid the bills and helped build a comfortable life for a family.

Those jobs got sent overseas – all because of corporate greed.

Wealthy billionaires and huge corporations have been destabilizing our communities just to line their own pockets.

This story is not unique. It’s not about left or right or even urban or rural. It’s happening more and more all across Wisconsin. Corporations are buying up farms and houses and leaving it on us to bear the burden.

The turning point in my life came for me in high school, when I lost my first friend to gun violence. As I got older, I lost more friends and saw more of my community struggling with similar tragedies. I recognized that this is happening too often in our communities – that we were experiencing far too much violence without enough systemic support.

And if the government can be quick to respond to the needs of the wealthiest individuals in this country, we should be even quicker to support the people who need our help the most.

These are the people who are ignored by our government time and time again.

It’s past time for that story to end — and as governor, I’ll deliver a bold vision for generational change here in Wisconsin. I’m glad to have shared part of my personal story with you, and if you’re ready to help support our movement, please chip in any amount today →

Folks: Donald Trump's so-called SAVE Act is Jim Crow 2.0 — and I just spent time on the Senate floor saying exactly that. Trump’s bill is a modern-day poll tax designed to make it harder for everyday Americans — particularly married women, veterans, Native Americans, and low-income voters — to cast a ballot. Trump’s bill is _not_ about election security. It forces every American to show a passport or birth certificate to register or re-register to vote. With current costs for these documents and wait times, this requirement would disenfranchise millions of voters. Women who changed their last name would need notarized affidavits. Veterans couldn’t use military IDs. Voter registration drives, online registration, and automatic registration would be gutted. **Our right to vote is the foundation of every other freedom we have. I have spent my career protecting that right, and I will not stop now.** [**Protecting the right to vote doesn’t just require a speech on the Senate floor. It requires sustained effort, resources, and everyday Americans — people like you who refuse to let Trump strip away our voices. | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127748517/609068673/623074613?refcode=jtk1447-fr-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjM3ODRjNzItYWUyNC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=33cLRYSbsjSLIj4ehnjLnF0kPnvgpd6vTc8iiiUoU5A=&emci=2f3b0309-9224-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=b3784c72-ae24-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=9329426)

Dear friend,

This week, I sat across from Markwayne Mullin, Trump’s new nominee to lead the Department of Homeland Security after Kristi Noem was fired, and asked him simple questions about requiring judicial warrants, body cameras, badges, and identification.
_He wouldn’t answer._
He deflected; he digressed; he gave me the non-answers that tells you exactly what this administration intends to do. And when the hearing was over, I walked out and said publicly what I knew to be true. Markwayne Mullin was equivocal and evasive and will not receive my support in his nomination.
This isn’t just a difference in procedure; these are your rights. This is about someone who will lead an agency that in the past year has sent masked men to people’s homes and, without a judge’s approval, forced their way in. Under Noem’s leadership they decided that an ICE officer's approval was enough. No court review. No oversight. Just random agents with a piece of paper they signed themselves.
Citizens have been swept up in these raids, with many ordinary people injured, families terrorized, and ultimately some have died. When I pressed Mullin on how he would reform the department, **he gave no accountability and no answer.**
And when it was over, the Republican-controlled committee voted to advance his nomination anyway.
That’s the fight we’re in right now: I’m slowing every nomination, I’m forcing votes, and I'm making sure every single Republican has to go on the record. But I can’t do it alone.
Friend, the full Senate vote on Mullin could come as soon as this weekend. When it does, I will be on that floor opposing him. I will be standing up for all Americans who deserve to feel safe, especially in their own home.
But the fight doesn’t end with Mullin, and Connecticut families deserve a Senator who will stand up to the Trump administration and their abuses of power. That’s exactly what I intend to do.

clean_body: Here’s why: | | | Dear friend, This week, I sat across from Markwayne Mullin, Trump’s new nominee to lead the Department of Homeland Security after Kristi Noem was fired, and asked him simple questions about requiring judicial warrants, body cameras, badges, and identification. He wouldn’t answer. He deflected; he digressed; he gave me the non-answers that tells you exactly what this administration intends to do. And when the hearing was over, I walked out and said publicly what I knew to be true. Markwayne Mullin was equivocal and evasive and will not receive my support in his nomination. This isn’t just a difference in procedure; these are your rights. This is about someone who will lead an agency that in the past year has sent masked men to people’s homes and, without a judge’s approval, forced their way in. Under Noem’s leadership they decided that an ICE officer's approval was enough. No court review. No oversight. Just random agents with a piece of paper they signed themselves. Citizens have been swept up in these raids, with many ordinary people injured, families terrorized, and ultimately some have died. When I pressed Mullin on how he would reform the department, he gave no accountability and no answer. And when it was over, the Republican-controlled committee voted to advance his nomination anyway. That’s the fight we’re in right now: I’m slowing every nomination, I’m forcing votes, and I'm making sure every single Republican has to go on the record. But I can’t do it alone. Friend, the full Senate vote on Mullin could come as soon as this weekend. When it does, I will be on that floor opposing him. I will be standing up for all Americans who deserve to feel safe, especially in their own home. But the fight doesn’t end with Mullin, and Connecticut families deserve a Senator who will stand up to the Trump administration and their abuses of power. That’s exactly what I intend to do. ### I've never looked back after defending our democracy on January 6.
| | [Harry Dunn](https://substack.com/@harryadunn)
---
| Mar 20
---
| [](https://substack.com/@harryadunn)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3102347&post_id=191605038&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkxNjA1MDM4LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc3NDA0NzkyMCwiZXhwIjoxNzc2NjM5OTIwLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMzEwMjM0NyIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.OPCiYNNrWZCpBvqAtAemz2r9PH1nQ_8zJsHaxslpjz4&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

---

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/44ca9e37-8a7c-4733-877e-de4af3b87d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I'll be straight with you: I've done a lot of tough things in my life. I played college football, tried to make it in the NFL. That was tough, mentally, physically, emotionally.

I served as a Capitol police officer for over 15 years, and those were tough some days.

But the aftermath of the January 6th insurrection was one of the toughest things I've been through. My pain and my trauma didn't end on January 7.

Even after the violence of that day, I dealt with death threats. I dealt with people harassing me for speaking out. And when I decided to testify in front of Congress? It was one of the toughest obstacles I've ever faced.
But I did testify, because it was my duty not just as an officer, but as an American. I made a big step the day I testified for the January 6th committee. I stepped in the direction of protecting our democracy.

**And honestly, I 've never looked back.**

**[I'm ready to protect our democracy as a Congressman, and I need you to join me ahead of my first and ONLY end-of-quarter deadline. I wouldn't ask if this fight wasn't absolutely critical - will you pitch in to my campaign and help me hit my 95,000 donation goal?](https://substack.com/redirect/44ca9e37-8a7c-4733-877e-de4af3b87d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[JOIN THE FIGHT](https://substack.com/redirect/44ca9e37-8a7c-4733-877e-de4af3b87d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
On January 6, 2021, I was at the Capitol, immersed in a profane mix of sweat, screams, shrieks, anger, fear, blood, death, broken limbs, spit, hatred, horror, racism, bigotry, and heroism.
Capitol and Washington Police officers fought for our lives, the lives of fellow police officers, and the nation's elected leaders - it didn't matter if they were a Republican, Democrat, or an Independent. They were the men and women we sent to Washington to govern our nation.
**It was my duty to protect them and our democracy.**
All the while, Donald Trump did nothing to help us. For hours after he incited the violence, we were beaten bloody. And some died.
That day was a stain on our nation. And we need to fight like hell to make sure we NEVER repeat a day like that.
**[I'll continue to use my voice to protect this country. I'll stand up to the lies, hate, and bigotry. I will always stand my ground to make sure democracy exists. But I need you to stand with me in this fight ahead of my biggest fundraising deadline yet:](https://substack.com/redirect/44ca9e37-8a7c-4733-877e-de4af3b87d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[JOIN THE FIGHT](https://substack.com/redirect/44ca9e37-8a7c-4733-877e-de4af3b87d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Together, we'll get through this nightmare to a better future.
-- Harry

For hours after he incited the violence, we were beaten bloody. And some died. That day was a stain on our nation. And we need to fight like hell to make sure we NEVER repeat a day like that. Together, we'll get through this nightmare to a better future. -- Harry You're currently a free subscriber to . To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM1NzQwNDgS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQyMTA5NTI3MgS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Support the Energy Bills Relief Act!

The Energy Bills Relief Act is a new, comprehensive bill cosponsored by over
half of House Democrats to rein in energy costs by prioritizing the clean,
affordable energy people in America need right now.

We deserve energy that doesn't make us sick, pollute our climate, or empty our
wallets. The Energy Bills Relief Act outlines a path that puts the needs of
people and our planet over polluter profits: ramping up clean energy like wind
and solar, holding data centers accountable, expanding heating assistance for
low-income families, and more — it’s a major step toward cutting climate
pollution and lowering utility bills for millions of people.

Add your name and show your support for the Energy Bills Relief Act! https://links.messages.lcv. ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv. Peter, Had enough of rising utility bills and threats to our environment at the hands
of the Trump administration? Us too. That’s why LCV is thrilled to announce the Energy Bills Relief Act.We’ve teamed up with climate leaders and activists on this new legislative
roadmap for bringing energy costs under control by prioritizing the clean,
affordable energy people in America need right now — all while building a more sustainable future. Show your support for the Energy Bills Relief Act — write to your member of Congress today! https://links.messages.lcv. The single most impactful thing we can do about skyrocketing energy costs is to
expand access to affordable, clean energy. And lucky for us and the planet, the
cheapest, most reliable forms of energy — such as wind, solar, and batteries —
are also the cleanest. We already have the tools to power our country with abundant, affordable, clean
energy — all made right here in America. And with the Energy Bills Relief Act,
we will have the necessary policies to relieve everyday people from suffocating
costs and pollution. The Energy Bills Relief Act will: Stop Trump propping up expensive, dirty fossil fuel power plants and attacking affordable, clean energy by reversing the administration’s roadblocks against the most inexpensive, clean, and safe energy sources. Make data centers pay their fair share of electricity bills, rather than burdening households and small businesses. Modernize and strengthen our electrical grid to ensure affordability, reliability, and sustainability in an era of skyrocketing bills, booming demand, and increasing disruptions from extreme weather. Help millions of low-income families pay for their utility bills by expanding the Low Income Heat Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) and the Weatherization Assistance Program. Restore the Inflation Reduction Act’s clean energy tax credits that Republicans eliminated in 2025, which jacked up electricity rates almost overnight. We deserve energy that doesn't make us sick, pollute our climate, or empty our
wallets. The Energy Bills Relief Act is a major step toward cutting climate
pollution and lowering utility bills for millions of people — and this is just
the beginning. LCV won’t stop fighting for the affordable, clean energy future
we all need and deserve. Thank you for taking action with LCV. Matthew Davis

These are KIDS. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127749447/609071493/-785282667?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYmQyNGNkNC1iMDI0LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hNEjod_cUhIBcl537gB-2vcrz9K7tCnGVJGKsxOONjw=)

Peter, It's Becca. **I’m furious that I even have to write this today but Republicans are pushing to deny immigrant children an education.** _These are kids_. Kids who want to learn. Kids who want to feel safe. Kids who deserve to walk into a public school without fear hanging over their heads. But right now, we are watching extremists try to turn immigrant children into political targets and I will not stand by and let that happen. [_**If you’re sickened by this attack on children, please click here and chip in today to help me fight back against this cruelty.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127749448/609071494/1043480310?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYmQyNGNkNC1iMDI0LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hNEjod_cUhIBcl537gB-2vcrz9K7tCnGVJGKsxOONjw=) **I’m a former middle school teacher, and I can tell you this: you learn a lot about what kids are carrying before they ever say a word.** You see it in their faces. You hear it in the way they hesitate. You feel it in the moments when a child is trying to focus, trying to be brave, trying to make it through the day while carrying far more than any kid should have to carry. Kids come into the classroom carrying hunger. Anxiety. Fear. Hope. The need to belong. And they need to feel seen. Public school should be a place that meets them with stability, support, and opportunity — not more fear. And yet that is exactly what Republicans are doing right now. They are targeting immigrant children and treating them like pawns in their sick political game. **It is cruel. It is dangerous. And it is deeply un-American.** I spoke out because I know what school means to a child. I know what a safe classroom can mean. I know what it means for a kid to have one place in their day where they can breathe, learn, and believe they matter. That is what public education is supposed to be. **So when politicians start arguing that some children are not entitled to that because of where they were born or who their parents are, we have to call this what it is: an attack on kids.** [_**If you’re with me here, chip in today to help me fight back against this attack on immigrant children and to defend public education.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127749449/609071495/1043480310?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYmQyNGNkNC1iMDI0LWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hNEjod_cUhIBcl537gB-2vcrz9K7tCnGVJGKsxOONjw=) Because kids today are already carrying so much. They are growing up with the fear of gun violence in schools.
They are living with the anxiety of climate change.
They are navigating loneliness, disconnection, and a world that too often makes them feel so small. And for immigrant kids, that fear is even heavier. Families are dealing with raids, intimidation, and the constant terror that their lives can be upended at any moment. **No child should have to live like that. No parent should have to drop their kid off at school wondering if fear will be waiting for them there. And no politician should be allowed to score points or keep their job by attacking children.** As a teacher, I learned that kids do better when they feel safe, when they feel supported, and when they know someone is fighting for them. **That is still what I believe. Hi Team, I’m reaching out about a race most people haven’t heard of, but one that powerful interests are pouring time and money into: **Arizona’s Salt River Project.** This public utility serves nearly 2 million people, and the decisions it makes will shape the future of clean energy, water use, and affordability in one of the hottest and fastest-growing states in the country. As you read this message, the far right, Trump-aligned organization Turning Point is organizing to elect a slate of MAGA-backed, fossil fuel-friendly candidates to these seats. We can’t let that happen. [I’ll be phonebanking with JanePAC’s endorsed candidates for the SRP Board on March 25 at 4pm PT / 7pm ET, and I’d love to see you there, Team. You can click here or use the button below to sign up to phonebank with us, or keep reading for more information.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127749709/609072460/-1406831908?refcode=ea.5c90933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.5c90933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjVjOTA5MzNkLWIxMjQtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=71exvQqYWCBk4nejr9iUOMS45wT29YOQN_6eundRb1k=&emci=5590933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=5c90933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105) | [**COUNT ME IN!**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127749711/609072462/-1406831908?refcode=ea.5c90933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.5c90933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjVjOTA5MzNkLWIxMjQtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=71exvQqYWCBk4nejr9iUOMS45wT29YOQN_6eundRb1k=&emci=5590933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=5c90933d-b124-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)
---
For years now, my Climate PAC has identified and invested in clean energy candidates running for Salt River Project leadership positions.
In 2024, we helped elect three incredible leaders to this very board because people across the country (like you) stepped up to help elect these leaders. Now, we need to do it again.
**And this time, we’re up against a coordinated effort from the far right.** If Turning Point and their allies buy these seats, it won’t stop here. It would only embolden their efforts in Arizona and future races across the country.
Like so many of the local races we get involved in, this could come down to just a handful of votes, especially in a system like Salt River Project’s, **where voting power is tied to land ownership, giving outsized influence to a small number of large property holders.**
So this moment matters.

name: Sarah McBride
subject: I want to be very clear about what’s at stake in the SAVE Act
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
The Senate is set to vote on the SAVE Act very soon.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=2981%2E21716%2E9jNm9u)
The Senate is set to vote on the SAVE Act very soon, and I want to be clear about what’s at stake.
Donald Trump and Republicans in Congress will tell you it’s about election integrity, but our elections are already incredibly secure. **The reality is they’re pushing this bill because they’re scared of losing in the midterms, and they want to make it harder for eligible Americans to register and vote.**
It’s a shame that Republicans would rather disenfranchise eligible voters than take the actions they need to lower costs and expand access to health care, but that’s where we are.
I was proud to vote against the SAVE Act in the House, and I’m urging my colleagues in the Senate to do the same.
Because ultimately, this is about who gets to participate in our democracy and who gets left out. And _no one_ who’s eligible to vote should be denied the chance to do so just because Republicans are scared of losing their majority.
I came to Congress to deliver for working families and protect our freedoms, and I intend to continue doing just that. But I can’t do this alone — in order to keep doing my job in Congress, I need your support.
[**That’s why I’m asking you to pitch in $5 or whatever you can right now to support my re-election campaign and help flip the House this November.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260320-1.Voyyzv&refcode=em20260320-2981&amount=5&t=2&akid=2981%2E21716%2E9jNm9u)

name: Dan Freeman
subject: We’re suing the Trump administration:
body:
The American people have a right to know whether the Trump administration plans to interfere with the midterm elections.
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-march-2026?amount=20&refcode=em_20260320_6460_fr&refcode2=6460_22930333_yFKCDU&akid=6460%2E22930333%2EyFKCDU)
---
Derek,
The DNC recently filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration under the Freedom of Information Act.
**We’re demanding transparency: If the Trump administration plans to interfere with November’s midterm elections, the American people have a right to know.**
In October, we sent 11 requests for information to the Justice Department, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Defense Department. Congress set a deadline for agencies to respond to information requests, and that deadline passed months ago. We’re done waiting.
President Trump has consistently attacked the integrity of American elections, in the courts and on the ground. The public has a right to know the administration’s plans for November.
We all remember President Trump asking Georgia’s secretary of state to “find 11,780 votes” after he lost by exactly that margin in 2020. More recently, President Trump told the _New York Times_ that he regretted not ordering the National Guard to seize voting machines in swing states he lost in the 2020 election. He’s even threatened to “nationalize” elections.
**The fact is, if the federal government is planning to deploy armed agents to the polls, we have a right to know. If they’re planning on sending troops, we have a right to know.**
That’s why we’re suing, Derek: to uncover any plans that the Trump Administration has failed to turn over, so the DNC can prepare for the fight ahead.
[**So if taking the Trump administration to court to force them to comply with the law is important to you, please consider chipping in $7 to the DNC today to help us continue our legal work and holding Trump accountable →**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-march-2026?refcode=em_20260320_6460_fr&amount=7&refcode2=6460_22930333_yFKCDU&akid=6460%2E22930333%2EyFKCDU)

The first $7,000 of each contribution from a person and the first $10,000 from a multicandidate committee (“PAC”) will be allocated to Cooper for North Carolina. The first $3,500 of a person’s contribution and the first $5,000 of a PAC’s contribution will be designated for the primary election; the next $3,500/$5,000 will be designated for the general election. The next $10,000 from a person and $5,000 from a PAC will be allocated to North Carolina Democratic Party – Federal. The next $44,300 of a contribution from a person and the next $15,000 from a PAC will be allocated to the DSCC General Fund. The next $132,900 from a person and the next $45,000 from a PAC will be allocated to the DSCC Headquarters Fund. The next $132,900 from a person and the next $45,000 from a PAC will be allocated to the DSCC Legal Fund. A contributor may designate his or her contribution for a particular participant. The allocation formula above may change if following it would result in an excessive contribution.

clean_body: Signing on is a small act that will make a huge difference. | | | | | Hey, Peter, we’re following up from yesterday. Donald Trump and the entire GOP establishment are firing on all cylinders to crush our grassroots movement, and we’re looking for 285 more signatures from your area before midnight to fight back and show our strength. Signing on is a small act that will make a huge difference. Thank you. Team Cooper \---------- Forwarded message ---------- From: Roy Cooper Date: Thur, Mar 19, 2026 Subject: Please endorse my campaign for U.S. Senate → | | | | Peter – over the past couple of weeks, I’ve been out on the road meeting with North Carolinians directly on the Make Stuff Cost Less tour. They tell me versions of the same thing: ⛽ Gas prices are spiking, and it’s costing more to put food on the table. 🩺 They can’t keep up with skyrocketing health insurance costs and get the care they need. 🇺🇲 They’re fed up with the chaos in Washington, DC, and they’re worried about the future of our country. I know we can do better. That’s why I’m in this fight. Before politics, before party and before power, I will always put the people of North Carolina first – as I’ve done my entire career in public service. As Governor: ✅ I expanded Medicaid for hundreds of thousands of working North Carolinians. ✅ I created hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs. ✅ I increased teacher pay and expanded paid parental leave. Now, I’m ready to fight in the Senate for working families – but getting there won’t be easy. The GOP is going all in to defeat me, and I need to know that folks like you are in my corner. | | Thank you, Roy Cooper | | Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here. National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us. Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.
